content: Older adults diagnosed with diabetes should adhere to an optimal nutritional plan that includes adequate protein intake to support their overall health. Engaging in regular physical activity is crucial and should include aerobic exercises, weight-bearing activities, and balance training to help maintain physical functionality and prevent decline. For older adults with type 2 diabetes who are also living with obesity, achieving a modest weight loss of approximately 5–7% of their body weight is recommended. This level of weight reduction has been shown to improve quality of life and reduce cardiometabolic risks. Lifestyle management strategies, which encompass a balanced diet and regular exercise, are vital for older adults to prevent frailty, enhance muscle strength, and lower the risk of falls and functional impairments. These changes collectively contribute to an enhanced quality of life for older adults.
